purpose: The layout primitive, restricted to the token scales. Everything in the package is built on it, and it is the escape hatch when Stack, Grid and Card do not fit.

useInstead.when: you need a run of children with one gap
useInstead.use: Stack — reach for Box only when no named layout fits

useInstead.when: you need a reflowing set of tiles
you need a bordered surface with a heading

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for Box and BaseBox in this package.
decision.beforeTheRules: Box takes TOKEN NAMES; BaseBox takes raw CSS values. Reaching for BaseBox is a declaration that the scales do not cover your case — which should be rare and visible in review.

rules.because: Stack, Grid and Card carry spacing defaults that keep pages consistent; a Box does not

rules.if: you need a value the token scales do not have
rules.then: use BaseBox and expect to justify it
rules.because: it accepts raw CSS, so it is the one place a value can escape the design system

rules.if: you are setting a spacing, size, colour, radius, elevation, layer or type value
rules.then: pass a token name — padding="spacing.4", background="surface", zIndex="menu"
rules.because: the compiler checks it against the scale, so a stray padding="17px" is a type error rather than a silent escape

rules.if: you are setting a keyword property — display, position, overflow, flexDirection
rules.because: these have no scale behind them; only properties that take a VALUE are tokenised

rules.if: the value should change at a breakpoint, on hover, or via a descendant selector
rules.then: use a className and put it in CSS
rules.because: props become an inline style, and inline styles cannot express a media query, a pseudo-class or a descendant rule

constraints: A property must be owned by props OR by CSS, never both — the inline style wins, so a value set in both places is unreadable.
There is no responsive-array prop. Supporting padding={['spacing.2','spacing.4']} needs generated classes, which this package has no build step for.
Every DOM prop passes through: id, role, aria-*, data-*, onClick, tabIndex. A Box is never a barrier to an attribute.

composition.childrenContract: Anything. Box adds no wrapper of its own — it renders exactly the element named by `as`.
composition.notes: Use `as` to keep the semantics right: as="section", as="header", as="ul". Do not wrap a Box in a semantic element you could have named.

antiPatterns.dont: Passing raw values to Box — padding="12px", background="#fff"
antiPatterns.do: Pass a token name, or use BaseBox and say why
antiPatterns.why: Box exists to make the scale the only way in; a raw value here is a type error

antiPatterns.dont: Setting the same property in both a prop and the className's CSS
antiPatterns.why: the inline style always wins, so the CSS value is dead but still reads as live

antiPatterns.dont: Using BaseBox because Box would not take your value
antiPatterns.do: Check whether a token fits first, and add one to the scale if the value is genuinely part of the system
antiPatterns.why: each BaseBox escape is a value that will not follow a theme change

antiPatterns.dont: Reaching for Box to lay out page content
antiPatterns.why: those carry the spacing rhythm; a bare Box starts at zero and every caller re-invents it

examples.canonical:
<Box as="section" padding="spacing.4" background="surface" borderRadius="lg" display="flex" flexDirection="column" gap="spacing.2">
  {children}
</Box>

incorrect.why: raw values — pass padding="spacing.3" and background="navSurface"
the inline padding wins and the CSS one is dead; give the property one owner
